source_review.notes: Checked all twelve structured references. Current OCI Image and Distribution specifications support descriptors, manifests, indexes, configurations, layers, digests, registry transfer, tags/digests, and referrers. Approved SLSA 1.2 supports provenance, build levels, distribution, verification, signer/builder expectations, and subject binding. Current Sigstore documentation supports identity, issuer, bundle, signature, and digest-claim verification. Current Kubernetes documentation supports digest references, name resolution, pull policies, cache behavior, and pull failures. Current Docker guidance supports multi-stage builds, base selection, context exclusion, cache and package practices, CI, and digest pinning. SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH supports deterministic timestamp inputs without being presented as complete reproducibility. NIST SP 800-190 supplies container threat categories without being treated as current product configuration.

practitioner_review.notes: A practitioner can apply the artifact contract, controlled-input build, trusted-builder provenance, reproducibility checks, minimal runtime design, layer hygiene, SBOM and vulnerability policy, signature verification, per-variant gate, digest-preserving promotion, deployment observation, rebuild/revocation, and retention workflow.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter progresses from OCI graph semantics through identity, build, provenance, runtime, evidence, multi-platform qualification, promotion, deployment, response, and retirement. Ten examples are distinct; five exercises progress from artifact design through threat modeling, promotion, incident response, and safety-critical transfer, with complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
